name: irony
quote: I got the very thing I was trying to avoid.
description: Linking the perception of a particular discrepancy in expectations to broader implications, with the goal of pointing out a possible pattern of reality, often negative.
examples: The Titanic was said to be unsinkable, but sank on its first trip.

variations.name: perceived irony
variations.description: Irony may be obvious or subtle - someone points out a difference that suggests a more general hypothesis, inviting you to consider whether there's a link between them. Sometimes there may be a relation. Other times, the event may just be coincidence.

comparisons.description: There may be an element of 'surprise' in an ironic statement, but the focus of irony is primarily on what this unexpected event might mean in a larger context.

commentaries.quote: Irony aims to make a statement about reality from an event. On one hand, this is good - trying to find patterns in the world is what people do. On the other hand, a single event doesn't prove a more general pattern.
An ironic statement may be a spontaneous and honest observation. It may also seek to influence listeners, such as encouraging empathy or contempt.

conditions: Considering a particular discrepancy in expectations against broader implications.
Having a goal of pointing out a possible pattern of reality, often negative.
